property-explorer-staging.vercel.app -> 200, 1117 bytes, title 'Smart Site - Explore your property' - the SPA is served.

LESSON: A naive regex over a Cloud Run describe document matches every tag's OWN status.traffic[].url and fabricates reference hits. A reference scan MUST parse spec.template.spec.containers[].env[].value, not the document text.

`vercel env pull` writes an empty value for a sensitive/encrypted variable, keeping the NAME and dropping the value. Measured on these artifacts: 68 config variables across 29 project dirs are unreadable this way, including the `*_URL` variables in all three projects the dispatch named (property-explorer: HAUSKA_ENGINE_API_URL, MCP_URL; command-center: RETRIEVAL_API_KEY; cmdcenter: MCP_URL, MCP_ADMIN_KEY, RETRIEVAL_API_KEY). So a regex scan over pulled .env files cannot establish the ABSENCE of a tag URL - it returns 0 either way. An empty value in a pulled .env means 'unreadable (sensitive/encrypted), or empty-by-design, or genuinely empty', never 'absent'.

Do NOT count every empty pulled value as a blind spot. A `vercel env pull` also emits Vercel's own runtime/build vars - VERCEL_GIT_*, VERCEL_URL, VERCEL_TARGET_ENV, NX_*, TURBO_* - which are EMPTY BY DESIGN and are not secrets. A first pass here reported 755/1348 (56%) unreadable; excluding system vars the true figure is 68, i.e. 5% of all vars and 10% of real config vars. The error was in the direction of drama, which is still an error, and it had already been written into two artifacts before it was caught.

Verify a repoint of a tag that has a PROVEN consumer by probing the consumer's own backend seam, not the tag URL. A 200 on the tag URL says nothing about whether the consumer still works. Concretely: property-explorer-staging reaches cortex-api through the relative path /api/spine/cortex/api (from its served bundle), so POSTing to that path and getting a 400 VALIDATION ERROR FROM CORTEX-API proves the request crossed the tag and reached the upstream - a 4xx generated by the upstream is positive evidence of connectivity, while only a 502/503/504 or transport error is evidence of breakage.

Read the SERVED BUNDLE to find a frontend's real backend shape. `fetch(origin + '/assets/index-*.js')` then matching for run.app hosts / relative paths revealed cortexBase = '/api/spine/cortex/api' - a relative path, so no host is hardcoded and no config read-back is needed. Grep of the config would never have shown this.

A 503 whose body names a MISSING ENV VAR ('proxy not configured', 'missing: X|Y') is an APPLICATION response, not a gateway failure. Do not classify it as a dead upstream. Distinguish by body, not status code alone (here: property-explorer-staging lacks RETRIEVAL_API_KEY entirely while property-explorer production has it).

PowerShell string escaping silently breaks comparisons. `$v -eq '\"\"'` inside a nested quoted command does NOT compare against two quote characters, so `HAUSKA_ENGINE_API_URL=""` was reported as 'has-value' and briefly contradicted the correct Node analysis. When two checks disagree, the one passed through multiple layers of shell quoting is the suspect; re-run it as a script FILE.

The Vercel CLI's stored OAuth token (APPDATA/com.vercel.cli/Data/auth.json) EXPIRES, and the CLI refreshes it transparently while a raw `Authorization: Bearer <token>` call to api.vercel.com 403s with `invalidToken:true`. So 'the CLI works' does not imply 'the token in that file works'. Building a REST call on that file requires a fresh interactive `vercel login` first.

The close schema in the dispatch is checked by EXACT key name: scripts/queue/lib.mjs does `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(parsed, "leave_behind")`, so a close written with `leaveBehind` (camelCase) fails the dependency check and makes `release --as close` refuse, even though every other field is right. The skeleton's `contradicted` is a STRING, not an array.

A quote attributed to a source must be re-read at the source before it is filed. This lane filed a close asserting the dispatch said something at 'line 78' that the dispatch does not say anywhere - the dispatch never mentions the variable or the project in question. Grepping the dispatch for the quoted strings is a one-second check that would have caught it.
